steps.say: Program starts at main() and creates our Demo window.
"implements ActionListener" = a PROMISE: this class will have an actionPerformed() method.
REGISTER: tell the button "when you are clicked, call ME (this)". This is the link Source → Listener!
Button is added and the window is shown.
Java makes an ActionEvent (e) and AUTOMATICALLY calls actionPerformed(e). You never call it yourself.

answer_html:
Definition

An Event Listener is a Java interface (in java.awt.event or javax.swing.event) that listens for an event on a GUI component and runs code to respond to it.

Role of Event Listener

  • Connects the Event Source (like a button) to the response code.
  • Provides methods that run automatically when a specific event occurs.
  • Keeps UI design separate from event logic so code stays neat and easy to update.

Figure – Delegation Event Model

[Event Source (Button)] ---> [Event Object] ---> [Event Listener (Handler Code)]

Different Event Listeners in Java

ListenerUsed for
ActionListenerbutton click, menu click, pressing Enter in a text box
MouseListenermouse press, release, click, enter, exit
MouseMotionListenermoving or dragging the mouse
KeyListenerpressing, releasing, or typing a key
ItemListenercheckbox, radio button, dropdown item
WindowListeneropening, closing, minimizing, restoring a window
